quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What happens if you refuse to take an alcohol test when police suspect you of driving while intoxicated?

options.text: It is your right and there are no consequences.
It is recommended.
Your license will be suspended.
You will only receive a fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license will be suspended.
questions.explanation: In Texas, driving a car means you agree to take an alcohol test whenever police ask. You cannot be forced to take the test, but your license will be suspended immediately if you refuse.

questions.question: You should not park within ____ of a traffic control signal.

options.text: 50 feet
30 feet
35 feet
45 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 30 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 30 feet of a traffic control signal, such as a stop sign, flashing light, or yield sign. Parking in the wrong spot can cause accidents.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line down the middle. What does this tell you?

options.text: Traffic moves in both directions on this road.
This is a one-way road.
The road is being repaired.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in both directions on this road.
questions.explanation: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic signals at an intersection are not working?

options.text: Park your car off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you are doing.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat it like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop. When it is safe, proceed through with caution.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.
A blasting zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign means a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Letting your car run in the driveway.
Accelerating quickly.
Slowing down gradually.
Braking hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: When you brake suddenly, you use fuel accelerating back to speed. If you look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes, you avoid hard braking and use less fuel.

questions.question: What do downward-pointing triangle signs mean?

options.text: School zone ahead.
Yield to other traffic.
Construction zone ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-pointing triangle signs tell drivers to yield. You can go when the road is clear and safe.

questions.question: Why should you be extra careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming cars may not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing bicycles because the cyclist may have to swerve into traffic suddenly to avoid an object. Always drive carefully near cyclists.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting an expressway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: What are the consequences for a driver or passenger not wearing a safety belt?

options.text: There are no consequences.
Just a warning.
A fine for each person not wearing a safety belt.
Jail time.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fine for each person not wearing a safety belt.
questions.explanation: In Texas, drivers and passengers can be fined for not wearing a safety belt. Anyone 15 years or older can receive a citation. Children under 17 must be in a safety seat or safety belt. There are no exceptions to this law.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Prepare to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you can go, but you must slow down and be careful. Look both ways before entering the intersection.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they should:

options.text: Drive the same way as if they were calm.
Drive faster because they are more alert.
Calm down and focus before driving.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can distract you and make it hard to drive safely. Your mind may be focused on your feelings instead of the road. Take time to calm down before you start driving.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an on-ramp, a driver should:

options.text: Let drivers already on the highway go first.
Have the right-of-way.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will move lanes for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let drivers already on the highway go first.
questions.explanation: When you are on an on-ramp entering the highway, you must yield to traffic already on the highway. Merge safely when you have a clear space.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you're coming.
Drive in the bicycle lane to pass.
Slow down and give them plenty of space.
Speed up to get in front of them quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have less protection than drivers. Slow down and give bicyclists as much room as you can. Passing too fast or too close can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the narrow bridge ahead.
The bridge ahead is one-way only.
Only one car can cross the bridge at a time.
The bridge ahead is too narrow to pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead is too narrow to pass a truck.
questions.explanation: This is a warning sign. It tells drivers that an upcoming bridge is narrow and you may not be able to safely pass a truck there. Slow down and be careful.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop. Stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When you are going through an intersection.
When you are passing a bicyclist.
When a child is about to run into the street.
When you are parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a child is about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others if they don't see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your car.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes that travel in the same direction. Broken white lines mean you can cross to pass. Yellow lines separate lanes that travel toward each other in opposite directions.

questions.question: When making a right turn, you should not:

options.text: Signal to other drivers.
Swing too wide for your lane.
Slow down.
Move to the far right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swing too wide for your lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down and use your turn signal before turning right. Stay in your lane and do not turn too wide, as this can hit other vehicles.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
A special speed zone.
A roadway with rules about stereo volume.
A TV show.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have large blind spots. These spots are on the sides, rear, and front. Other vehicles cannot be seen in these areas. These blind spots are called the "No zone."

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Intersection ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is coming from both directions ahead.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians. If you think another driver might hit you, sound your horn to alert them.

questions.question: In an accident, what information should you provide?

options.text: Your insurance and registration information.
Your full name and address.
Reasonable assistance to anyone who has been injured.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before leaving an accident scene, you must give your name, address, registration, and insurance information to other drivers. You must also help anyone who is injured.

questions.question: What must a driver do when dealing with pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian knows you are there.
Always give them the right-of-way, even if they are breaking the law.
Give them the right-of-way only when it is legally their turn.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give them the right-of-way, even if they are breaking the law.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what. Always watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light is used at dangerous intersections. Treat it the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: When can you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you lose control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: It is appropriate to use your horn when you lose control of your vehicle. Sound your horn to warn other drivers.

questions.question: In Texas, when must drivers use their headlights?

options.text: When they are tired.
When their vehicle has a problem.
30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.
During the day in clear weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.
questions.explanation: You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise. Slow down when driving at night and only go as fast as you can see ahead.

questions.question: What do diagonal stripes sloping down to the right on a barricade mean?

options.text: You must stop.
You should steer to the right.
You should steer to the left.
You should drive straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should steer to the right.
questions.explanation: Diagonal stripes on a barricade show you which way to go. Stripes sloping down to the right mean steer right. Stripes sloping down to the left mean steer left.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
You can drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. You must use headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if safe to do so.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and keep driving at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if safe to do so.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, slow down and change lanes if you can do so safely. If there is only one lane or changing lanes is unsafe, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much space as possible.
